jobs.description:
The group you’ll be a part of

The Corporate Strategy Group charts our course for long-term profitable growth. This team drives Lam in the development of and alignment to our strategic priorities and key initiatives. Additionally, they oversee Lam's Corporate Development team and Lam Capital, which makes investments that help fuel technologies of the future.

The impact you’ll make

As a member of the Lam Corporate Strategy team you will be responsible for driving and orchestrating projects focused on leading Lam to make the best strategic choices in support of our corporate objectives.

What you’ll do

- Take ownership of significant portions of strategy development and generate creative, action-oriented insights and recommendations.
- Facilitate joint problem-solving with mid-level and senior-level business partners.
- Distill information, gain clarity of ideas, synthesize insights, and define next steps for execution.
- Produce novel research work products, often challenging existing company strategies with new insights.
- Deliver timely and impactful recommendations, ensuring the organization is engaging in the right strategic discussions.
- Synthesize data to identify trends and insights, and proactively identify and close gaps in the collective knowledge base.
- Understand and stay current with the competitive landscape.
- Author and deliver high-impact presentations and plans to senior management.

Typical Projects Include
- Analysis of ecosystem and competitive trends to identify growth opportunities and disruptive threats.
- Development of detailed growth strategies, with sufficient depth to undergo stress testing and integration into the corporate planning process.
- Critical, insightful analyses of Lam and its ecosystem that deliver actionable strategic options.

Who we’re looking for

- Typically requires a minimum of 12 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 8 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 5 years experience; or equivalent experience.
- Semiconductor industry experience.

- Excellence in structured thinking, with superior analytical capabilities (both quantitative and qualitative).

- Ability to identify and define business questions and issues, and develop strategic, analytical, and financial frameworks to help drive strategic debate.

- Exceptionally strong personal initiative, sound business instincts, and comfort working in environments with high levels of ambiguity.

Preferred qualifications

- Strong understanding of Lam, its ecosystem, and the trends that are and will shape its future.
- Creative, out-of-the-box thinker who is intellectually curious and demonstrates a continued interest in learning.
- Ability to manage multiple simultaneous high-priority projects, often including project management of cross-functional teams.

jobs.title: Skills Architect Program Manager
jobs.description:
The group you’ll be a part of

The Global Human Resources Group operates on the understanding that our people are our most valuable assets. They think globally to optimize our workforce, integrate our Core Values into everything we do, and deliver the HR solutions to enhance the employee experience and enable future growth.

The impact you’ll make

The Skills Architect Program Manager is responsible for designing, governing, and continuously evolving Lam Research’s enterprise skills architecture. This role owns the structure and integrity of the skills framework, including skills taxonomy, role-based skills profiles, proficiency models, skill definitions, and relationships across jobs, learning, talent, and workforce processes.

The role combines skills architecture expertise with program management to translate workforce, business, and labor market insights into scalable skills solutions. The role leads skills validation, develops taxonomy recommendations, establishes architecture standards, and manages the implementation of approved changes across various talent and learning platforms. The role also surfaces actionable skills insights and data to identify workforce capability needs and inform broader upskilling and reskilling efforts across Lam.

What you’ll do

Skills Architecture & Governance
- Design and continuously evolve Lam’s enterprise skills architecture, including taxonomy structure, proficiency levels, definitions, relationships, and role-based skills profiles.
- Establish architecture standards and governance criteria for creating, modifying, consolidating, and retiring skills.
- Analyze business needs, workforce priorities, and labor-market trends to identify emerging, declining, and critical skills.
- Maintain the quality and integrity of the skills taxonomy by resolving duplicate, outdated, overlapping, or poorly defined skills.
- Evaluate proposed changes and recommend scalable enhancements aligned with enterprise standards and business requirements.
- Maintain architecture documentation, decision rationale, and quality controls.

Skills Program Management
- Lead enterprise skills architecture priorities and roadmap initiatives.
- Plan and facilitate skills discovery, design, and validation sessions with business and functional stakeholders.
- Translate business requirements and SME input into architecture recommendations, decisions, and implementation plans.
- Maintain the roadmap, backlog, dependencies, decision log, and implementation priorities.
- Monitor adoption, assessment, and taxonomy-health data to improve the skills framework and employee experience.
- Analyze and surface skills insights, gaps, and trends to inform enterprise upskilling and reskilling priorities.

Ecosystem Integration
- Define how enterprise skills architecture is represented across Lam, independent of any specific technology platform.
- Establish skills-mapping principles across jobs, learning content, development plans, career pathways, talent acquisition, and workforce planning.
- Partner with HRIS and technology teams to translate architecture requirements into system configurations and integrations.
- Assess the downstream impact of taxonomy changes and validate skills tagging, content mapping, recommendations, and role profiles across systems.
- Identify and resolve architecture and data inconsistencies between platforms.

What you’ll do (continued)

Stakeholder Partnership
- Serve as the enterprise subject-matter expert for skills architecture, taxonomy design, and role-based skills modeling.
- Advise HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Workforce Planning, Talent Management, Global Inclusion Learning & Development, HRIS, and business leaders on skills architecture decisions.
- Facilitate alignment between business needs, enterprise standards, governance requirements, and system constraints.
- Translate complex architecture concepts into clear recommendations for business and executive audiences.

Success Measures
- Quality, consistency, and scalability of the enterprise skills architecture
- Accuracy and relevance of skills taxonomy and role-based profiles
- Successful implementation and adoption of approved architecture enhancements
- Alignment of skills across talent, learning, career, and workforce processes
- Timely delivery of roadmap priorities, architecture decisions, and actionable skills insights that inform upskilling, reskilling, and workforce capability priorities

Who we’re looking for

- Minimum of 12 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 8 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 5 years experience; or equivalent experience.
- 5+ years of experience in skills architecture, talent management, job architecture, workforce development, learning, HR technology, or a related field.

- Experience designing or significantly enhancing enterprise skills frameworks, taxonomies, or role-based skills models.

- Experience translating business and workforce requirements into scalable skills solutions.

- Experience facilitating skills discovery and validation with SMEs, HR partners, and business leaders.

- Strong analytical, consulting, program-management, and executive-communication capabilities.

- Experience working across interconnected HR, talent, and learning platforms.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with Eightfold, Cornerstone, Workday, SuccessFactors, or similar platforms.
- Experience designing skills taxonomies, proficiency frameworks, and relationships among skills, roles, jobs, and learning content.

As a Data Operations Analyst at Lam, you will play a pivotal role in enabling organizational efficiency and effectiveness across the Global Planning organization. This role focuses on improving how teams access, manage, interpret, and act on information by strengthening systems capability, analytical maturity, and data-driven operating discipline.

- Lead and participate in projects to resolve problems or to support continuous process improvement.
